constraint_decided_it: E29 Design or Procedure -- 'documented plans for the execution of actions ... for shaping or guiding the execution of an instance of E7 Activity', example 'the ISO standardisation procedure' -- plus P33 used specific technique (E7 -> E29). E29 is in the 241-item core ontology, so a documented retention schedule has a core-CRM home; both answers discarded it. A discarded it by conflating E29 with the failed 'Activity Plan' subclass proposal, which is a non sequitur.
better_modelling: Split the case three ways instead of two. (1) The retention schedule is a documented procedure: E29 Design or Procedure (E29 sits in the core ontology; cf. its own example 'the ISO standardisation procedure'), attached to the review activity by P33 used specific technique (domain E7, range E29) -- and E87 Curation Activity's scope note explicitly presupposes 'an implicit or explicit curation plan', which is that object. (2) The disposal review, once performed, is an E87 Curation Activity or E13 Attribute Assignment (both subclasses of E7): P14 carried out by the records officer (E39), P17 was motivated by (domain E7, range E1) the statute (E31/E30) or the curatorial assessment, P2 has type (E1 -> E55) distinguishing statutory requirement from curatorial judgement, and P70i is documented in / P141 assigned onto the file. (3) Only the forward-looking 'next review date' is genuinely outside CRMbase: Issue 166 states 'dealing with instances of E4 in the future (if they exist at all) will be subject of extensions of the CRM, and not part of the scope of CRM', and Issue 333 placed Activity Plan / Event Specification (of future event) in CRMsoc, later CRMact v0.2 (Issue 419). So the honest answer is 'the schedule and the completed review are documentable in CRMbase; the scheduled future date is not', not 'all of it belongs to another system'.
reasoning: A's t0483 quote is verbatim, but the source does not support the use made of it: Ore's message is a wording correction ('the "is intended" has to be replaced by "was intended"'), not a rejection, and A's claim that the 2012 follow-up 'is likewise still unresolved' is contradicted by Issue 333 (Done, 2019, Activity Plan into CRMsoc) and Issue 419 (CRMact v0.2) -- two misattributions of what the archive says, which is `unsupported` regardless of the conclusion. A also rejects E29 itself on the strength of the failed Activity Plan proposal, discarding the one core class that fits, and reads t0603 (Henttonen simply asking whether anyone else is building such a model) as 'the community's own answer'. Every source B cites checks out verbatim -- Issue 166's E4-in-the-future clause, t0608, t0731, Issue 333's CRMsoc outcome, and the Introduction > Scope line 'the curated, factual knowledge about the past at a human scale' that B hedged as unverified -- and B correctly separates the completed review (E7/E13, P17) from the future date. B is still suboptimal: its E29 rejection ('not a scheduling rule tied to calendar review dates') reads the scope note too narrowly against E29's own procedure example and against E87's 'implicit or explicit curation plan', it cites E87 and Issue 161 without using them, and P13 destroyed has range E18, so it cannot attach to the E31 file it proposes.
